description: Restructure the README into an English baseline README.md and a Japanese README.ja.md, each with a language-switcher link as the first content line, matching the reference repo's pattern. Replace the ASCII architecture block with an '## Architecture' section that embeds docs/architecture.png and links the editable .drawio and the .svg (in BOTH files). Preserve all existing substantive content, split by language. Keep the product name 'AI Monster / AIモンスター'.
steps: Read the current README.md (bilingual single file, 218 lines, H1 '# AIモンスター / AI Monster 🥚🐉'). Inventory every section so none is dropped: overview/features, architecture (ASCII block + monorepo table), growth stages & Bedrock model mapping table, prerequisites (incl. Bedrock model access + region), deploy (one command path, the auto-wire config.json explanation, reading the outputs table), overriding Bedrock model IDs (env + CDK context, ALLOWED_ORIGIN, .env.example link), local development, teardown, build & deploy status, directory layout, the Kiro Challenge note, and the SUBMISSION.md link.
Study .tmp-ref/README.md and .tmp-ref/README.ja.md for the switcher wording and the '## Architecture' section wording to mirror the convention.

Rewrite README.md as the ENGLISH baseline. First content line (immediately after the H1 title) MUST be the switcher exactly: '**English** | [日本語](README.ja.md)'. Translate all existing substantive content to English-primary prose while preserving every section and all technical specifics (model IDs, env var names, commands, tables, SUBMISSION.md link). Keep the product name as 'AI Monster' (title may remain 'AIモンスター / AI Monster' or English-first per the reference's bilingual-title style, but do NOT reintroduce 'Digital Monster'). Keep the repo token 'kiro-digitalmonster', package names (@ddm/*), and infra identifier 'DigitalMonsterStack' / stack-based names exactly as they are (these are not the product name).

In README.md, replace the old ASCII architecture code block with an '## Architecture' section: a line like '![Architecture](docs/architecture.png)', then 'The editable diagram is [`docs/architecture.drawio`](docs/architecture.drawio) (open with draw.io / diagrams.net). A PNG (`docs/architecture.png`) and vector (`docs/architecture.svg`) are included.', followed by bullet points describing THIS flow (Browser -> CloudFront -> private S3 via OAC; SPA reads config.json then calls API Gateway HTTP API; 4 Lambdas getMonster/saveMonster/battle/chat; single DynamoDB table; ONLY chat calls Bedrock with Claude tier by growth stage; AWS CDK one-command deploy). Keep the monorepo packages table.

Create README.ja.md as the JAPANESE version. First content line MUST be the switcher exactly: '[English](README.md) | **日本語**'. Move the existing Japanese content here (the current README is already largely Japanese, so this is mostly relocation + ensuring every section is present), with the same '## アーキテクチャ / Architecture' or '## Architecture' section embedding ![Architecture](docs/architecture.png) and linking docs/architecture.drawio and docs/architecture.svg, replacing the ASCII block. Preserve all sections and technical specifics.
Ensure both files reference the image path as docs/architecture.png (relative, repo-root-based) and the links as docs/architecture.drawio and docs/architecture.svg so they resolve on GitHub.
Verify no section was dropped from either language file versus the original, and that the SUBMISSION.md link is present in both.
git add README.md README.ja.md and commit on docs/architecture-and-readme, e.g. 'docs: split README into EN baseline + README.ja.md and embed architecture diagram'.
acceptance_criteria: README.md is English-baseline and its first content line after the H1 is exactly '**English** | [日本語](README.ja.md)'.
README.ja.md exists, is Japanese, and its first content line after the H1 is exactly '[English](README.md) | **日本語**'.

Both README.md and README.ja.md contain an Architecture section with '![Architecture](docs/architecture.png)' and links to docs/architecture.drawio and docs/architecture.svg; neither contains the old ASCII architecture diagram block.

All substantive sections from the original README are preserved across the two files (overview, features, growth stages/model mapping, prerequisites incl Bedrock model access, deploy incl config.json auto-wire + outputs, overriding model IDs, local dev, teardown, build/deploy status, layout, SUBMISSION.md link).

Product name is 'AI Monster / AIモンスター'; the string 'Digital Monster' is NOT reintroduced as the product name (repo token kiro-digitalmonster, @ddm/* package names, and DigitalMonsterStack infra identifier remain unchanged).
The embedded image path and switcher links are valid relative paths that resolve from the repo root on GitHub.
verification: head -n 5 README.md shows the H1 then '**English** | [日本語](README.ja.md)' as the first content line
head -n 5 README.ja.md shows the H1 then '[English](README.md) | **日本語**' as the first content line
grep -F '![Architecture](docs/architecture.png)' README.md and README.ja.md both match
grep -F 'docs/architecture.drawio' and grep -F 'docs/architecture.svg' match in both READMEs
grep -n 'ブラウザ (React' README.md README.ja.md returns nothing (old ASCII block removed) — or confirm by reading that no ``` ASCII arch diagram remains
grep -F 'SUBMISSION.md' README.md and README.ja.md both match
grep -ni 'Digital Monster' README.md README.ja.md returns no occurrence used as the product name (only acceptable in unchanged identifiers if any; prefer none)
export PATH="/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH" && npm run build && npm run test both still exit 0 (docs-only change did not break baseline)
findings: Split the single bilingual README into an English-baseline README.md and a Japanese README.ja.md on branch docs/architecture-and-readme (commit 4f64df2). Both keep the shared H1 '# AIモンスター / AI Monster 🥚🐉'. First content line after the H1 is the switcher exactly: README.md '**English** | [日本語](README.ja.md)', README.ja.md '[English](README.md) | **日本語**'. The old ASCII architecture code block (under '## 🏗️ アーキテクチャ / Architecture') was removed in both files and replaced with an '## Architecture' / '## 🏗️ アーキテクチャ / Architecture' section embedding ![Architecture](docs/architecture.png), a line linking [`docs/architecture.drawio`](docs/architecture.drawio) (draw.io/diagrams.net) plus the PNG+SVG mention (translated for the JA file), then bullet points describing the real flow: Browser(React+Vite SPA, EN/JA i18n) -> CloudFront (HTTPS,OAC) -> private S3 (BlockPublicAccess all) holding dist/+config.json; SPA reads /config.json then calls API Gateway v2 HTTP API (CORS); 4 Lambdas getMonster(R/W)/saveMonster(W)/battle(R/W)/chat(R+Bedrock); single DynamoDB table DigitalMonsterStack-Monsters (PK=id, PAY_PER_REQUEST); ONLY chat calls Amazon Bedrock (bedrock:InvokeModel scoped to Claude inference-profile ARNs) with Claude tier by stage (baby=none/canned, rookie=Haiku, champion=Sonnet, ultimate=Opus); AWS CDK (TypeScript) one-command deploy. All sections preserved and split by language with no drops: overview/features; growth stages & Bedrock model mapping table (us. model IDs intact); prerequisites (incl. Bedrock model-access enablement + region us-east-1); deploy one-command path (npm install -> npm run build -> cd infra -> cdk bootstrap -> cdk deploy); config.json auto-wire explanation; Outputs table (CloudFrontUrl/ApiUrl/BucketName/TableName); overriding Bedrock model IDs (env vars + CDK context, ALLOWED_ORIGIN, .env.example link); local development; teardown; build & deploy status; directory layout; Kiro University Challenge note; SUBMISSION.md link (present in both). Monorepo packages table kept in both. Product name stays 'AI Monster / AIモンスター'; no 'Digital Monster' product-name string reintroduced (only the DigitalMonsterStack / DigitalMonsterStack-Monsters identifiers and infra path remain, which are not the product name). The reference .tmp-ref/ was absent so I re-fetched daichiasada/kiro-worldriskmap README.md via gh to mirror switcher placement and Architecture wording, then removed .tmp-ref before committing. Sanity gate (docs-only): `npm run build` (shared->backend->frontend->infra) and `npm run test` both green — all 47 node:test cases pass, exit 0. Only README.md and README.ja.md were committed; no files under packages/ or infra/ were modified.
